name: TX-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes it one of the reddest seats in the country
Ronny Jackson's overwhelming financial edge: $5.4 million on hand versus $2,800 for Mark Nair
Prediction markets price Jackson's win probability near 96-97%
Incumbency and absence of any polling or expert ratings suggesting competitiveness
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: a deep-red R+23 district, a well-funded incumbent with no serious financial counterweight, and markets pricing a near-certain Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings indicating vulnerability, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly twenty points for Jackson stands.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Jackson or a dramatic national wave exceeding anything in recent cycles is the only plausible path to putting this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 13th District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and incumbent Ronny Jackson is seeking another term with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean of roughly R+23 sets a steep floor for any Democrat, and Jackson has raised nearly $4.8 million with $5.4 million on hand, dwarfing challenger Mark Nair's $138,000 raised and just $2,800 in cash. No public general-election polling exists for the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 96% chance of winning, aligning closely with the underlying fundamentals. Nair would need an extraordinary, district-spanning wave to close a gap this wide. The forecast expects Jackson to win by roughly twenty points, reflecting the district's lean tempered slightly by the national political environment. Barring an unforeseen shock, this seat remains safely in Republican hands.
